question.text: Expense Ratio of 1.5% on an MF returning 12% gross, net return is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Mutual fund costs and expenses are deducted in arriving at net assets and NAV, so investors earn the gross return less the expense ratio. Net = Gross - TER = 12% - 1.5% = 10.5%. The Trap: 12% is the pre-expense (gross) return, 13.5% incorrectly adds the expense ratio, and 1.5% is the expense ratio itself rather than the net return. Note: Net return to investors is defined in the workbook as the return after fees and expenses; always compare schemes on a net-of-expenses basis when assessing performance.
